full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff's case was that they acquired the suit lands covering three khatians namely, C. S. Khatian Nos. 55, 71 and 75 by auction purchase and they obtained delivery of possession of the same. The defendants having dispossessed them from C. S. plot No. 747 of C. S. Khatian No. 71, the plaintiffs filed a suit under Section 9 C. P. C. being Title Suit No. 108 of 1958 against the defendants for recovery of the said plot which was however dismissed. Thereafter, in April, 1959 the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs from the rest of the suit lands. Hence the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and for mesne profit relating to the lands of the aforesaid three khatians namely C. S. Khatian No. 55, 71 and 75. 

 3. Upon a consideration of the evidence on record the learned Munsif decreed the suit in respect of the lands of Khatian No.71 and 75 but dismissed the suit relating to the lands of Khatian No. 55 and also rejected the prayer for mesne profit. Against the judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif two appeals were filed; one by the plaintiffs against the dismissal of their suit in respect of Khatian No.55 and another by the defendants in respect of decree passed by the learned Munsif relating to the Khatiang No.71 and 75. Both the appeals were heard together and the learned Subordinate Judge by his judgment and decree dismissed both the appeals filed by the plain tiffs and the defendants and affirmed the findings of the learned Munsif in respect of C. S Khatian No.71 and 75. Hence the presen appeal at the instance of the defendants. 

 9. Apart from these, I find that the learned Subordinate Judge has not taken into consideration some of the documentary evidence filed on behalf of the defendant-appellants namely exhibit B which was the certified copy of the decree passed by the learned Munsif in a civil suit under Section 9 C.P.C. between the parties in respect of C.S. Khatian No. 75. The suit was dismissed in favour of the defendants. The suit was not only between the same parties but also related to the same suit land. The certified copy of the judgment in the said suit was filed by the plaintiffs and it has been marked as exhibit 9(a). But that exhibit also has not been considered by the learned Subordinate Judge. Then there is exhibit C(1) which of course was a judgment in a criminal case between the parties under sections 447 and 147 B. P. C. over the same suit land in which the defendants were acquitted on the finding that they were in possession. Whatever may be the evidentiary value of the criminal court judgment, none of the courts below seem to have taken any notice of the said judgment. Since it was admitted in evidence and marked as an exhibit it ought to have been considered by the courts below particularly when the question of possession and dispossession was a vital issue in the suit. It has been held by the Privy Council in the case of Dinomoni Chowdhurani Vs. Brojo Mohini Chowdhurani, in I.L.R. 29 Calcutta at page 187 that orders passed under Section 145 Cr.P.C. are admissible in evidence on general principles as well as under Section 13 of the Evidence Act to show who the parties to the dispute were, what the land in dispute was and who was declared to be entitled to possession.
